The card counts every self-loop edge in the graph: 2 + 1 = 3." width="100%"} A self-loop is an edge where the source and target are the same node. This counts all self-loop edges in the entire graph, regardless of which nodes they belong to. Use `count_loops()` to get per-node counts. Self-loops are common in state machines, reflexive relationships, and chemical reaction networks. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of edges where source equals target. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two of these three edges connect a node to itself, so `count_all_loops()` reports `2`: ::: {#3628964d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("A", "A"), # self-loop ("B", "B"), # self-loop ] ) ) graph.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Self-loops stack: adding two self-loops on the same node counts both: ::: {#6f32d78e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_edge("A", "A") graph.add_edge("A", "A") graph.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
